rows.title: Toxic culture is the norm at the FDIC, outside review cites 500 employee complaints
rows.standfirst: A law firm investigation of the FDIC documents a toxic workplace culture where hundreds of employees complained of sexual harassment, discrimination and other misconduct.

rows.title: Hazard maps: The curse of knowledge
rows.standfirst: What happens when small town politics collide with the climate crisis? And how do hazard maps—maps that show which homes in your neighborhood are at risk of getting destroyed or damaged by a natural disaster—come into play? On today's episode, how some people—from Indiana to Oregon to Alaska—are facing some very real concerns about insurance and the ability to sell their houses.

rows.title: TikTok challenges U.S. ban in court, calling it unconstitutional
rows.standfirst: The high-stakes legal battle could determine the future of the popular app in the U.S. TikTok's legal filing calls the ban law an unprecedented violation of First Amendment rights.

rows.title: Neoliberal economics: The road to freedom or authoritarianism?
rows.standfirst: Nobel-winning economist Joseph Stiglitz's new book argues the road to tyranny is paved not by too much, but by too little government.

rows.title: The clock is ticking to fix Social Security as retirees face automatic cut in 9 years
rows.standfirst: Social Security's finances have improved slightly in the last year. But the popular retirement program still faces big challenges including the threat of automatic benefit cuts in less than a decade.

rows.title: How Colorado towns are trying to get some water certainty
rows.standfirst: In Western Colorado, towns and farms are banding together to pay a hundred million dollars for water they don't intend to use. Today on the show, how scarcity, climate change and a first-dibs system of water management is forcing towns, farms and rural residents to get spendy.

rows.title: FAA is investigating Boeing for apparent missed inspections on 787 Dreamliner
rows.standfirst: The FAA says Boeing informed the agency in April that required inspections to confirm that the wings were properly bonded to the carbon fiber fuselage on certain 787 jets were not completed.

rows.title: How a stretch of I-20 through Alabama tells the story of American workers
rows.standfirst: In recent years, Alabama workers have found themselves at the center of three high-profile labor campaigns in three industries. How those have unfolded tells us a lot about labor in America today.

rows.title: Women no longer have to make the first move on Bumble. Will it make the app better?
rows.standfirst: Bumble, known for allowing women to message men first, unveiled new features that allow men to make the first move. Will the change breathe new life into online dating, and the company's stock?

rows.title: China makes cheap electric vehicles. Why can't American shoppers buy them?
rows.standfirst: American drivers want cheap EVs. Chinese automakers are building them. But you can't buy them in the U.S., thanks to tariffs in the name of U.S. jobs and national security. Two car shoppers weigh in.

rows.title: NASA's chief is worried about China getting back to the moon first. Here's why
rows.standfirst: NASA Administrator Bill Nelson told NPR he sees the U.S. in an urgent race with China to find water on the moon, and that he trusts SpaceX, despite Elon Musk's increasingly controversial profile.

rows.title: Possible TikTok ban could be 'an extinction-level event' for the creator economy
rows.standfirst: Tens of thousands of people earn a living on TikTok. But as creators face down the real possibility of TikTok going away, many are trying to switch to new platforms to save their livlihoods.

rows.title: 'Zillow Gone Wild' brings wacky real estate listings to HGTV
rows.standfirst: Zillow Gone Wild started in 2020 as an Instagram account devoted to eccentric property listings. The show focuses on homes that defy everyday expectations in some way.

rows.title: More than 16,000 pounds of ground beef sold at Walmart recalled over E. coli risk
rows.standfirst: Cargill says that, out "of an abundance of caution," it is recalling several of its ground beef products produced in late April and sold at Walmart locations across the eastern U.S.

rows.title: Not too hot, not too cold: a 'Goldilocks' jobs report
rows.standfirst: It's Jobs Friday and the jobs report is in! There's more jobs! ... but not as many as expected. And there's a teensy bit more unemployment and slower wage growth. But there's an upside ... Plus, healthcare is growing like gangbusters and how immigrants affect American-born workers.

rows.title: DOJ says Boeing broke deal that avoided prosecution after 2 fatal 737 Max crashes
rows.standfirst: Boeing has violated the terms of a deal to avoid prosecution after the fatal crashes of two 737 Max planes more than five years ago, the Department of Justice told a federal judge on Tuesday.

rows.title: The "Winner Take All" problem
rows.standfirst: When June Carbone, Naomi Cahn and Nancy Levit set out to write a book about women in the workforce, they initially thought it would be a story all about women's march towards workplace equality. But when they looked at the data, they found something more disturbing: of the ways in which women's push toward workplace equality has actually been stalled for years.

rows.title: More Americans are falling behind on credit card bills
rows.standfirst: Credit card delinquencies rose in the first three months of the year. That's a sign of the growing financial stress that some families are feeling in an era of rising prices and high interest rates.

rows.title: 5 takeaways from Biden's tariff hikes on Chinese electric vehicles
rows.standfirst: The Biden administration is quadrupling tariffs on China-made EVs. The tariffs are part of a broad swath of protectionist policies first imposed by former President Trump.

rows.title: Legal experts say a TikTok ban without specific evidence violates the First Amendment
rows.standfirst: The Justice Department is expected to argue that its clamp down on TikTok is about national security, but Constitutional lawyers say there is no way around grappling with the free speech implications.

rows.title: Fallout continues from the Miss USA resignations as a runner-up declines the crown
rows.standfirst: After a pair of resignations rocked the pageant world, organizers have found a replacement for Miss USA but not Miss Teen USA. Last year's runner-up said this week that she turned down the crown.

rows.title: It was a classic rap beef. Then Drake revived Tupac with AI and Congress got involved
rows.standfirst: AI can conjure the voice or likeness of a dead celebrity with just a few clicks. This opens a host of legal questions about the rights of the deceased and their heirs to control their digital replicas

rows.title: Biden announces new tariffs on imports of Chinese goods, including electric vehicles
rows.standfirst: President Biden is keeping the tariffs on Chinese imports put in place by his predecessor and 2024 opponent, former President Donald Trump. And he's adding new ones for things like electric vehicles.

rows.title: Is 'government crypto' a good idea?
rows.standfirst: Advancements in cryptocurrency networks are sparking conversations about the potential for Central Bank Digital Currencies, or CBDCs for short. Advocates for CBDCs think they would provide security and unlock more efficient fiscal policy actions. However, opponents believe they would provide a shortcut for government interference and the erosion of privacy.

rows.title: Melinda French Gates resigns as co-chair from the Gates Foundation
rows.standfirst: French Gates says she is "immensely proud" of the work of the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation, and the decision to step down as co-chair was not easy. Her last day is June 7.

rows.title: GameStop surges after meme stock investor 'Roaring Kitty' resurfaces online
rows.standfirst: Shares in the video game retailer more than doubled at one point after a prominent meme stock investor made his first online posting in about three years.

rows.title: With 'bleisure' and fewer workers, the American hotel is in recovery
rows.standfirst: A new type of traveler is part of the post-pandemic reset at U.S. hotels, along with fewer daily cleanings and pancake-slinging machines.

rows.title: Auto workers in Alabama are voting on joining a union. Here's what you need to know
rows.standfirst: Workers at Mercedes-Benz in Alabama start voting this week on whether to join the United Auto Workers union. Last month, Volkswagen workers in Tennessee voted overwhelmingly to unionize.

rows.title: A federal judge temporarily halts U.S. plan to lower credit card late fees to $8
rows.standfirst: The temporary injunction imposed by Judge Mark Pittman in the Northern District of Texas is a win for the big banks and major credit card companies. The plan was set to go into effect next week.

rows.title: Biden will keep Trump's China tariffs, and add new ones on electric vehicles
rows.standfirst: The Biden administration is finally wrapping up its review of President Donald Trump's tariffs on Chinese imports. It will keep those tariffs, and add more on things like electric vehicles.

rows.title: AI Tupac and the murky legality of digital necromancy
rows.standfirst: With a few clicks of AI software, anyone can conjure the voice or visual likeness of a dead celebrity — or really anyone. This new world has opened up a bunch of new legal questions about the rights of people and their heirs to control digital replicas of themselves. Today on the show, how a Drake diss track featuring the voice of Tupac made it into the Congressional record, and how it may lead to more regulation of AI.

rows.title: Target is cutting prices on 5,000 items including milk, butter and pet food
rows.standfirst: Target joins other retailers trying to draw inflation-weary shoppers to stores. The chain says reductions have already been reflected in about 1,500 products.

rows.title: Biden will name new boss soon to lead 'toxic' FDIC
rows.standfirst: FDIC chairman Martin Gruenberg says he's prepared to step down once a successor is confirmed. Gruenberg has been widely criticized for fostering a toxic workplace at the agency.

rows.title: Scarlett Johansson says she is 'shocked, angered' over new ChatGPT voice
rows.standfirst: Johansson says she was approached multiple times by OpenAI to be the voice of ChatGPT, and that she declined. Then the company released a voice assistant that sounded uncannily like her.

rows.title: Building generational wealth in rural America
rows.standfirst: Homes are not just where we eat and sleep, but one of the primary ways people build generational wealth in the U.S. But with home shortages and harsh climates, rural America's path to building that wealth looks a little different than other parts of the country. Today on the show, we focus in on housing challenges in Alabama's Black Belt and one innovative solution to preserving generational wealth.

rows.title: Red Lobster files for bankruptcy after missteps including all-you-can-eat shrimp
rows.standfirst: The seafood chain is in hot water after a series of bad choices by a parade of executives. Almost 580 restaurants will stay open, after dozens closed abruptly last week.

rows.title: 'Magic United': Disneyland characters vote to unionize
rows.standfirst: Disneyland employees in California, including those who perform as characters from Mickey Mouse to Moana, have voted to unionize. The 1,700 workers will be represented by Actors' Equity Association.

rows.title: The hack that almost broke the internet
rows.standfirst: Last month, the world narrowly avoided a cyberattack of stunning ambition. The targets were some of the most important computers on the planet. Computers that power the internet. Computers used by banks and airlines and even the military.

rows.title: Mercedes workers vote no to union. UAW says they were illegally intimidated
rows.standfirst: More than 5,000 Mercedes-Benz workers who build luxury SUVs in Alabama were eligible to vote on whether to join the UAW. Workers faced intense anti-union messaging from Mercedes in the run-up.

rows.title: How the Dominican Republic became Latin America's economic superstar
rows.standfirst: For decades, the Dominican Republic's economy has been growing at a remarkably steady pace. The Caribbean nation of 11 million people is today considered a middle-income nation, but the International Monetary Fund projects it could become an advanced economy within the next 40 years.

rows.title: Biden ending new leases in America's top coal region
rows.standfirst: Citing climate change, federal land managers are moving to end new leasing for coal in the country's top producing region.

rows.title: The Dow Jones hits 40,000 for the first time. What to know about this major milestone
rows.standfirst: Stock markets received a boost from new data showing inflation is easing. Lower inflation has raised hopes about the U.S. economy — but there are still a lot of unknowns.

rows.title: Supreme Court upholds funding structure for consumer watchdog agency
rows.standfirst: The opinion was written by Justice Clarence Thomas, who reversed the decision of the 5th Circuit. Justices Neil Gorsuch and Samuel Alito dissented.

rows.title: With flyers more distracted than ever, United rolls out a rebooted safety video
rows.standfirst: United Airlines is releasing a new safety video for the first time in years. The refresh comes as airlines struggle to hold the attention of passengers who are distracted by screens of their own.

rows.title: The highs and lows of US rents
rows.standfirst: The latest inflation numbers are in. This month's Consumer Price Index, or the CPI, is ... well, good and bad news for renters. Shelter prices went up over the last year, but at a slower pace. Shelter makes up nearly a third of the CPI. Today's episode: Rent. Where is it high? Where is it low? What exactly is "coffee milk"? The Indicator tours the U.S. to bring you the answers.

rows.title: Voice analysis shows striking similarity between Scarlett Johansson and ChatGPT
rows.standfirst: A new lab analysis conducted for NPR by Arizona State University data scientists shows that OpenAI's "Sky" voice is more similar to Johansson's than hundreds of other actors analyzed.

rows.title: How the FBI's fake cell phone company put criminals into real jail cells
rows.standfirst: There is a constant arms race between law enforcement and criminals, especially when it comes to technology. For years, law enforcement has been frustrated with encrypted messaging apps, like Signal and Telegram. And law enforcement has been even more frustrated by encrypted phones, specifically designed to thwart authorities from snooping.

rows.title: Summer box office woes: Hollywood's optimistic, but movie seats are still empty
rows.standfirst: After an already-slow spring, movie theater attendance over Memorial Day Weekend was the lowest in decades, apart from 2020.

rows.title: 'Buy DJT' is a new rallying cry for Trump supporters
rows.standfirst: Shares of Trump Media, the company behind Truth Social, were volatile a day after his historic conviction. It's an early test of how committed his supporters will actually be in owning the shares.

rows.title: Fax machines permeate Germany's business culture. But parliament is ditching them
rows.standfirst: Four out of five companies in Europe's largest economy continue to use fax machines. But Germany's parliament has until the end of June to stop relying on the antiquated communication technology.

rows.title: Indicator Quiz: May Edition
rows.standfirst: It's time for The Indicator Quiz!

rows.title: 'Wall Street Journal' layoffs continue, despite lucrative AI deal and record profits
rows.standfirst: The Wall Street Journal conducted another round of layoffs, explaining that it was pulling back from regional and local general news. It already has cut staff in Washington and abroad.

rows.title: 1.5 million adult bed rails are recalled following 2 reports of entrapment deaths
rows.standfirst: The Consumer Product Safety Commission says users of Medline's “Bed Assist Bars" can become entrapped within the bed rail or between the product and the side of a mattress when it's attached to a bed.

rows.title: Boeing promises big changes as the plane maker looks to rebuild trust and quality
rows.standfirst: Troubled plane maker Boeing promised sweeping changes to its manufacturing operations in an action plan that was mandated by federal regulators after a midair blowout on a 737 Max jet in January.

rows.title: What happens after you get scammed? Can you get your money back?
rows.standfirst: We are living in a kind of golden age for online fraudsters. As the number of apps and services for storing and sending money has exploded – so too have the schemes that bad actors have cooked up to steal that money. Every year, we hear more and more stories of financial heartbreak. What you don't often hear about is what happens after the scam?

rows.title: Using anecdotes to predict recessions
rows.standfirst: Eight times a year, we award regional Federal Reserve Banks with our coveted Beigie Award. While the anecdotes within the Beige Book offer us fascinating looks into the economy, to others, it can be difficult to make anything of the stories they tell. That's why we're giving out a special Beigie award today to some economists who found a way to use anecdotes to peer into our economic future.

rows.title: American Airlines faces a discrimination suit after removing 8 Black men from flight
rows.standfirst: Neither passenger knew each other, nor were they seated together on the Jan. 5 flight from Phoenix to New York. A lawsuit alleges they were removed from the flight after a complaint about body odor.

rows.title: Lending to family or friends? Don't be afraid to ask for your money back
rows.standfirst: Our audience shares their perspective on the tricky etiquette of loaning money to friends and family.

rows.title: Can dental therapists fill the gap in oral care?
rows.standfirst: Dental therapists have been practicing in other parts of the world for decades, but in the U.S. they are relatively few and far between. Like a hygienist, dental therapists can do cleanings as well as some procedures usually reserved for dentists, like simple extractions. They could also be the solution to getting underserved, rural communities better oral care. Today on the show, new momentum for dental therapy and why the American Dental Association is pushing back.

rows.title: Melinda French Gates to give $1 billion to women's rights groups
rows.standfirst: The 59-year-old says her decision to donate $1 billion was in part due to the racial gap in women's mortality rates. She most recently stepped down as co-chair of the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation.
